Marcos Jr., ITO ang TUNAY na state of the nation. Dalawang araw matapos ang SONA, pinapasinungalingan ng #CarinaPH ang mga salita ni Marcos.

Wala ni anino ni Marcos, Duterte, at ng kanilang flood control projects ang makita ngayong nasa state of calamity ang Metro Manila.

Nauna nang umalis ng bansa si VP Sara Duterte kaninang umaga kasama ang kaniyang pamilya papuntang Germany. Iniwan niya ang walo na patay, dalawang sugatan, isang nawawala sa Northern Mindanao, at 866,483 na pamilyang apektado dahil sa bagyo. Kalakhan ng apektado ay mga maralitang lungsod, manggagawa, magsasaka, at mangingisda. Ang pinsala sa agrikultura ay nasa P8.7 million at pinsala sa imprastraktura ay umabot na sa P700,000.

Ipinagmalaki ni Marcos ang di umanong natapos na 5,500 flood control projects sa kanyang State of the Nation Address (SONA) noong isang araw ngunit pareho pa rin ang dinaranas ng mamamayang Pilipino: lubog sa baha, nasa panganib, at kanya-kanyang paraan para iligtas ang sarili. Ang ganitong mga proyekto ay kadalasan pang balon ng korapsyon at hindi komprehensibong tinutugunan ang climate change.

Ang pagtindi ng pagbaha ay idinulot ng walang pagkukubling pagbebenta ni Marcos ng mga lupain, kabundukan, at dagat ng Pilipinas. Isa na rito sa porma ng malawakang reclamation projects na sumisira sa ating kalikasan tulad na lamang ng Manila Bay Reclamation project.

Dapat managot ang rehimeng Marcos sa kriminal na kapabayaan nito at lantarang paglulustay ng pera ng bayan para sa ganansya ng mga kapitalista at dayuhan. Simbolo ang pag-alis ni Sara Duterte papuntang Germany at kawalang aksyon ng rehimeng Marcos sa gitna ng sakuna na hindi kailanman sila tunay na nagsisilbi sa bayan, kundi para lang sa kanilang sarili at mga imperyalistang amo.

Flooded Car? Here's what to do:

1. Immediately disconnect the negative cable of your car battery to avoid any possible short circuit. This is also to protect the ECU or computer box from damage.

2. Do not start the engine. Try to push the car out to higher ground or try jacking it with the car jack.

3. Disengage and release the parking brake. Keep the transmission in 1st gear (for manual transmission) or "P" (for automatic transmission) to prevent the brake canvas from sticking. This is even more important for cars that use drum brakes.

4. Take plenty of photos both inside and outside the car to document any damage or how deep the car was underwater. This will be useful for both the Insurance and/or Professional Mechanic to determine the extent of the damage.

5. Wait at least 24 hours before you do anything to the vehicle, giving it time to drain, if not completely dry out.

6. If the water got so deep that the dashboard was covered, do not try to start it at all. If any liquid is in the cylinders it will cause damage to the engine. Most of the electronics in the car would have been submerged at this depth, as well.

7. If you don’t think the water got that high, it’s still best to take a look at the oil dipstick to see if there are any traces of water in the lubrication system. If so, assume the engine is flooded and don’t try to start it.

8. You’re in better shape if the water stayed below the center line of your wheels. Nevertheless, let the interior air out as much as possible before trying to start it, taking out the floor mats, trunk mat and even the seats. Much of the wiring and some of the computers in today’s cars are located under the carpet and console box, so even if the engine compartment was not inundated, you could still experience faults to secondary systems.

9. When in doubt, either have your vehicle towed to your trusted service center or call your professional mechanic/electrician for a more thorough inspection and assessment.

🌂 Leptospirosis is a disease caused by Leptospira bacteria. Infected animals spread the bacteria through their urine (pee). When infected animals pee, the bacteria get into the water or soil and can live there for weeks to months.

🌂 You can be infected if you touch fresh water, soil, or other objects contaminated with infected animal urine. The most common ways to get infected is urine or contaminated water getting in your eyes, nose, mouth, or broken skin (such as a cut or scratch). You can also get infected by eating contaminated food or drinking water.

🌂 Some people with leptospirosis do not have any symptoms. When symptoms occur, they can include fever, headache, chills, muscle aches, vomiting, jaundice (yellow eyes and skin), red eyes, stomach pain, diarrhea, and sometimes a rash. 

🌂 Without proper treatment with antibiotics, people with leptospirosis may develop serious problems with their kidneys, liver, or lining of the brain and spinal cord. In some cases, leptospirosis can cause death.

𝙒𝙃𝙊 𝙄𝙎 𝘼𝙏 𝙍𝙄𝙎𝙆?
✔️ Visit flooded or recently flooded areas
✔️ Swim, wade, kayak, or raft in potentially contaminated fresh water like lakes and rivers
✔️ Visit urban areas with poor sanitation
✔️ Touch animals or their body fluids. Animals that can be infected are mammals, including rodents, cows, sheep/goats, pigs, horses, dogs, and wildlife.

Flooded Car? Here's what to do:

1. Immediately disconnect the negative cable of your car battery to avoid any possible short circuit. This is also to protect the ECU or computer box from damage.

2. Do not start the engine. Try to push the car out to higher ground or try jacking it with the car jack.

3. Disengage and release the parking brake. Keep the transmission in 1st gear (for manual transmission) or "P" (for automatic transmission) to prevent the brake canvas from sticking. This is even more important for cars that use drum brakes.

4. Take plenty of photos both inside and outside the car to document any damage or how deep the car was underwater. This will be useful for both the Insurance and/or Professional Mechanic to determine the extent of the damage.

5. Wait at least 24 hours before you do anything to the vehicle, giving it time to drain, if not completely dry out.

6. If the water got so deep that the dashboard was covered, do not try to start it at all. If any liquid is in the cylinders it will cause damage to the engine. Most of the electronics in the car would have been submerged at this depth, as well.

7. If you don’t think the water got that high, it’s still best to take a look at the oil dipstick to see if there are any traces of water in the lubrication system. If so, assume the engine is flooded and don’t try to start it.

8. You’re in better shape if the water stayed below the center line of your wheels. Nevertheless, let the interior air out as much as possible before trying to start it, taking out the floor mats, trunk mat and even the seats. Much of the wiring and some of the computers in today’s cars are located under the carpet and console box, so even if the engine compartment was not inundated, you could still experience faults to secondary systems.

9. When in doubt, either have your vehicle towed to your trusted service center or call your professional mechanic/electrician for a more thorough inspection and assessment.

I'm sharing (just in case) my notes from PBBM's third State of the Nation Address (SONA), which was delivered yesterday, July 22, 2024, at the Batasang Pambansa Complex in Quezon City. Despite the threat of Severe Tropical Storm Carina and the absence of the Vice President, this historic event appeared to have the greatest confirmed attendance in Philippine history.

Major Highlights:

1. AGRICULTURE AND FISHERIES:

   - Highest rice harvest in the past year.
   - Ready to release the ASF vaccine.
   - Support for fishermen: 500 million fingerlings and 3,000 boats provided.
   - Distribution of 130,000 land titles to beneficiaries.
   - Seizure of PHP 2.7 billion worth of smuggled agri-fisheries products.

2. INFRASTRUCTURE AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE:

   - Completion of 1,200 kilometers of farm-to-market roads.
   - Irrigation for almost 45,000 hectares of new land.
   - Philippines secured a seat in the Loss and Damage Fund board.
   - Construction of 100 evacuation centers.
   - 5,500 flood control projects completed.

3. TECHNOLOGY AND CONNECTIVITY:

   - Over 10 million devices benefited from free internet.
   - Completion of Phase 1 of the National Fiber Backbone.
   - Transmission line inaugurated in Central Luzon for grid reliability.
   - Cebu-Negros-Panay backbone project completed for Visayas power supply stability.

4. HEALTH AND EDUCATION:

   - Increased availability of generic medicines (from 21 to 53) in PhilHealth.
   - Bridging the digital gap alongside the classroom gap.
   - Expanded career progression system for public school teachers.

5. ECONOMIC INDICATORS:

   - Employment rate increased to 95.9 percent.
   - Graduates produced through the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program.

Sinabi ng mga senador na naniniwala sila na ang reclamation project sa Manila Bay ang naging sanhi ng baha hanggang tuhod sa labas ng Senado sa Lungsod ng Pasay noong Miyerkules.

Sa isang text message sa mga mamamahayag, sinabi ng dating Senate President Juan Miguel Zubiri na naniniwala siyang ang reclamation ay isa sa mga dahilan kung bakit binaha ang bahagi ng Diokno Boulevard.

“This, I believe, is the consequence of all the reclamation happening in Manila Bay, wala ng malabasan na flood water dito sa Pasay at Manila,” ayon kay Zubiri

“Babaha at babaha na palagi dyan sa atin tuwing uulan nang malakas,” dagdag niya.

Sinisi rin ni Sen. Joel Villanueva ang reclamation project para sa malawakang pagbaha sa Bulacan, ang kanyang bayan.

“Reclamation pa more!” ayon sa kanyang mensahe sa mga mamamahayag.

Matatandaang naging mainit na balita sa panahon ni dating Pangulong Rodrigo Duterte ang pag-apruba niya sa mga reclamation projects sa Manila Bay. 

Noong taong 2023, napagpasyahan ng gobyerno ni Pangulong Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. na suspendihin ang lahat ng 22 Manila Bay reclamation projects na na naaprubahan sa panahon ni Duterte.
